Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 31, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Luqman, because it includes the name of Luqman the Wise, mentions some of his story and wisdom, and the etiquette with which he disciplined his son.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• It points to the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and the loftiness of its meanings, and that it is guidance and mercy. It also points to a group of wretched people who cast the Qur'an behind their backs and exchanged the flutes of Satan for the verses of the Qur'an.

• It mentions the signs of dazzling power in this finely ordered universe, which indicate the oneness of the Great Creator, and it rebukes those who worship other than the Creator, glorified and exalted is He.

• It explains what a father should be toward his son, through the story of Luqman with his son. Within it are upbringing, guidance, and sound counsel, which are among the effects of the wisdom that God bestows on whomever He wills of His servants.

• It mentions the abundant blessings of God upon His servants, which necessitate worshipping Him and thanking Him, and it follows this with mention of the people of disbelief and denial, who worship other than God out of imitation of their fathers.

• It commands fear of the Day of Recompense, on which the strongest bonds of affection between father and son, and son and father, will vanish, and it warns against falling into the snares of Satan, being deceived by his embellishment, and being deceived by this world and its adornments.

[Tafsir]

﴿Alif Lam Meem﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been covered at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah.
These are the verses of the Qur'an, the book full of wisdom.
These verses are guidance and mercy for those who do good deeds by acting on what Allah sent down in the Qur'an, and on what His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) commanded them.
Those who perform the prayer completely at its appointed times, and give the obligatory zakat to its rightful recipients, and who are certain of the resurrection and recompense in the Hereafter.

Those are the ones characterized by the attributes mentioned earlier, who are upon clear guidance from their Lord and light. And those are the ones who will be successful in this world and the Hereafter.

Among people is one who buys idle talk, meaning everything that distracts from obedience to God and diverts one from seeking His pleasure, in order to lead people astray from the path of guidance onto the path of desire. He takes God's signs as a mockery. For such people is a punishment that will humiliate and disgrace them.

When Our verses are recited to him, he turns away from obedience to Allah and becomes arrogant, not heeding them, as if he had not heard anything, as if there were deafness in his ears. So give him good news, O Messenger, of a painful, agonizing punishment in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 31, verse 8:

Indeed, those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did the righteous deeds that they were commanded to do, for them are everlasting bliss in the Gardens.

Their life in those gardens will be an everlasting life that does not end and does not pass away. Allah has promised them this as a true promise. He, glorified is He, never breaks His promise, and He is the Mighty in His command, the Wise in His management.

God created the heavens and raised them up without pillars, as you can see them. He cast firm mountains upon the earth, so that it would not shake and move and thereby ruin your lives. He spread across the earth all kinds of creeping and moving creatures. And We sent down water from the clouds, and with it We caused to grow on the earth every beautiful pair, useful and pleasing to the eye.

All that you see is the creation of Allah. So show me, O polytheists: what have your gods that you worship besides Allah created? Rather, the polytheists are in clear error, straying far from the truth and uprightness.

We gave Luqman, a righteous servant of Ours, wisdom, which is understanding of the religion, intelligence, and correctness in speech. We said to him: ﴿Give thanks to Allah﴾ for His blessings upon you. Whoever gives thanks, his thanks benefits only himself, and whoever denies His blessings, then Allah is free of need of his thanks, not in need of it, and deserving of all praise and commendation in every state.

Remember, O Messenger, the advice of Luqman to his son when he said to him, admonishing him: "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association with Allah is a great wrong, and it is among the greatest and most heinous of major sins."

We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents and good treatment of them. His mother bore him, weakness upon weakness, and his weaning from breastfeeding was completed within two years. We said to him: Be thankful to Allah, and then be thankful to your parents. To Me is the final return, and I will recompense each one according to what they deserve.

If they strive with you, [O believing son], to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them, but keep company with them in this world with kindness, in matters that involve no sin. And follow the path of one who has turned back from his sin and returned to Me, and who believed in My Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do in the world, and I will recompense every doer for his deed.

O my son, indeed if a deed, whether good or bad, were the weight of a mustard seed, and it were within a rock or anywhere in the heavens or in the earth, Allah would bring it forth on the Day of Resurrection and call the doer to account for it. Indeed, Allah is Subtle (Latif) toward His servants, Acquainted (Khabir) with their deeds.

O my son, establish the prayer completely, with its pillars, its conditions and its obligatory parts; enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, gently, softly and with wisdom, according to your capacity; and bear patiently whatever harm befalls you in return for your enjoining good and forbidding evil. And know that these admonitions are among the matters that Allah has commanded, which one should be keen to uphold.

"And do not turn your face away from people out of contempt, nor walk through the earth arrogantly and boastfully. Indeed, Allah does not love every self-deluded, boastful person in his bearing, his manner and his speech."

And be modest in your walk, and lower your voice, and do not raise it. Indeed, the most hateful and detestable of voices is the voice of donkeys, which are known for their stupidity and their loud braying.

Have you not seen, O people, that Allah has made subservient to you whatever is in the heavens, such as the sun, the moon and the clouds, and other things besides these, and whatever is on the earth, such as animals, trees and water, and other things beyond counting? He has showered upon you His blessings, both apparent in your bodies and limbs, and hidden in your minds and hearts, and what He has stored up for you that you do not know? Yet among mankind is one who disputes concerning the Oneness of Allah and sincere worship of Him, without any proof or clear explanation, and without a clear Book that sets out the reality of his claim.

When it is said to these disputers, who argue against the Oneness of Allah and His being singled out for worship: "Follow what Allah has sent down to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)," they say: "Rather, we will follow what our fathers were upon, of polytheism and the worship of idols." Would they do that even if Satan were calling them, by adorning for them the evil of their deeds and their disbelief in Allah, to the punishment of the blazing Fire?

Whoever submits his worship entirely to Allah and directs his intention to his Lord, the Most High, while being excellent in his words and perfecting his deeds, has then grasped the most trustworthy means leading to the pleasure of Allah and His Paradise. And all matters return to Allah alone, so He will reward the one who does good for his good, and the one who does evil for his evil.

And as for whoever disbelieves, do not let his disbelief grieve you, O Messenger; and do not be saddened. For you have discharged what was incumbent upon you of the call and the conveyance (of the message). To Us is their return and their final destination on the Day of Resurrection, and We will inform them of their evil deeds which they committed in the world, and then recompense them for them. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of what their breasts conceal of disbelief in Allah and preference for obedience to Satan.

We will grant them enjoyment in this perishable world for a brief period. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, We will compel them and drive them toward a terrible punishment, which is the punishment of Hell (Jahannam).

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 31, verse 25:

And if you were to ask them, O Messenger, those who associate partners with Allah: "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." So when they say that, say to them: "All praise is due to Allah, who has made the proof against you manifest from yourselves. But most of these polytheists do not reflect or contemplate who it is that deserves all praise and thanks, and so they associated others with Him."

To God, glory be to Him, belongs everything in the heavens and the earth, as its owner, its servants, its creation and its ordaining. Therefore none deserves worship besides Him. Indeed God is the One free of need from His creation, and all praise and commendation are His in every state.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 31, verse 27:

Even if all the trees on earth were made into pens, and the sea, with seven more seas added to it, were ink, the words of Allah, of His knowledge and His judgment, and what He revealed to His angels and messengers, could not be exhausted. The pens would break and the ink would run out, yet the perfect words of Allah, which no one can encompass, would not be exhausted. Indeed Allah is Mighty in His retribution against those who associate others with Him, Wise in the management of His creation. The verse establishes that speech is an attribute of Allah, -exalted is He-, in its true reality, as befits His majesty and perfection, glory be to Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 31, verse 28:

Your creation, O people, and your resurrection on the Day of Judgment are, in ease and facility, no different than the creation of a single soul and its resurrection. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing of your utterances, All-Seeing of your deeds, and He will recompense you for them.

Have you not seen that Allah takes from the hours of the night, so the day lengthens and the night shortens, and He takes from the hours of the day, so the night lengthens and the day shortens? He has subjected the sun and the moon for you, each of them running in its orbit until a known, specified term, and that Allah is Aware of all the deeds of creation, whether good or evil, nothing of them hidden from Him?

This is all from the greatness of Allah's power, so that you may know and affirm that Allah is the Truth in His essence, His attributes, and His actions, and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and that Allah is the Most High in His essence, His rank, and His dominion, above all His creation, the Great over everything, and everything other than Him is subject to Him. So He alone is deserving of being worshipped, to the exclusion of anyone else.

Have you not seen, O observer, that the ships sail upon the sea by the command of Allah, as a blessing from Him to His creatures, so that He may show you some of His signs and proofs that you may take heed? Indeed, in the sailing of ships upon the sea are signs for every steadfast one who restrains himself from what Allah has forbidden, who obeys Him, and who accepts His decrees, and grateful for His blessings.

When the polytheists board ships and the waves rise over them from every side like clouds and mountains, fear and terror of drowning overtake them, so they turn to God, making their supplication sincerely to Him alone. But when He brings them safely to land, some of them are moderate, not fulfilling the thanks owed to God in full; and some of them are disbelievers who deny His blessings and refuse to acknowledge them. None deny Our signs and proofs, which point to the perfection of Our power and Our oneness, except every treacherous one who breaks his covenant and is ungrateful for the favours of God upon him.

O people, fear your Lord and obey Him by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. Beware of the Day of Resurrection, on which no parent will avail his child and no child will avail his parent in anything. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, without doubt. So do not be deceived by the worldly life and its adornments, lest they make you forget the Hereafter. And let no deceiver deceive you about Allah, from among the devils of the jinn and mankind.

This is the commentary on surah 31, verse 34 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

Indeed Allah, alone without any other, knows when the Hour will come to pass. It is He who sends down the rain from the clouds; none besides Him can do that. He knows what is in the wombs of females, and He knows what every soul will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in which land it will die. Rather, Allah Most High alone is singled out with the knowledge of all of that. Indeed Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware, encompassing the apparent and the hidden; nothing of them is hidden from Him.
